note: Per-package coverage floors for github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go, replacing the single 60% repository floor the coverage job in .github/workflows/ci-go.yml enforced until 2026-10-15. Measured 2026-10-15 with GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.4 (the toolchain line in go.mod) on INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C (2 vCPU), linux/amd64, with: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.4 go test -coverprofile=coverage.out -covermode=atomic ./... Percentages are statement coverage summed per package directory by scripts/checkcov, not go tool cover -func, whose per-function percentages cannot be aggregated into per-package statement coverage. The measurement runs under the toolchain go.mod pins on purpose: statement counts move between Go minor versions (go1.27 counts the server package ~4.5 points lower than go1.25.4), and both `make coverage` and CI set GOTOOLCHAIN from go.mod the same way. Each floor is the measured percentage rounded down to the nearest 0.1: the 0.1 is slack against toolchain drift, and a floor nobody can meet gets raised away. Raising a floor needs a fresh measurement in the reason; lowering one needs a fresh measurement named in the commit body. Packages with no tests by design are listed under excluded with a reason, never given a floor of zero. The e2e, cmd/soroauth and rpcflow entries were re-measured on 2026-10-16 with the same command and toolchain; the numbers before that re-measurement and what moved them are in the commit that changed them.

policy.text: Floors are set from measurement. The signing path (the root package and internal/xdrcopy) carries floors strictly above the 60% repository-wide floor this scheme replaced, so a regression in the path that produces signatures cannot hide behind a repository average. Coverage is not correctness: it says which lines ran, not that the result is right — the mutation-testing work is the stronger check; these floors are a tripwire for regressions, not evidence of correctness.

github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go.reason: the signing path: Preimage/Payload, AuthorizeEntry, the guards and the sentinels; a wrong byte here moves money

github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/cmd/diff.reason: generates the differential corpus JS and Python must reproduce; its arms and seeds run only here

github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/cmd/soro.reason: the CLI is the documented surface for payload, sign, simulate and submit; parsing regressions reach users first

github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/e2e.reason: the untagged half of the e2e harness: which network, which funding endpoint and which results file a run uses, decisions that a normal `go test ./...` exercises even though the scenarios themselves need the e2e tag and testnet

github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/internal.reason: the exported-doc-comment gate: a bug here silently stops enforcing documentation
the bounded-decoder gate: a bug here silently stops enforcing the input bound the newest code most needs
the signing path's deep copy: every entry-returning function goes through it and aliasing here mutates caller input

github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/remote.reason: the HTTP signing protocol: the server recomputes the digest and refuses a mismatch; that refusal is the safety property

github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/rpcflow.reason: the record/enforce RPC pass the CLI runs; a regression changes what callers submit to the network

github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/scripts/.reason: the per-package coverage gate itself: a bug here would pass the regressions it exists to catch
the documentation site generator and internal link/anchor checker: a bug here ships broken links or omits docs

github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/server.reason: the HTTP verification service: it must never report cannot-check as verified

excluded.github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/cmd/genc: dev tool, exercised by CI itself: CI regenerates the fuzz seed corpus and fails on drift
excluded.github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/examples: no tests by design: examples are documentation and are exercised by golden/e2e runs
no tests by design: examples are documentation and are exercised by golden/e2e runs
excluded.github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/internal: no tests by design: its snippets are owned by the root package's README/docs drift tests
excluded.github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go/scripts/: dev tool, exercised by CI itself: the bench job runs it on every push to main
dev tool, exercised by CI itself: run inside an old release's worktree to generate the frozen set (testdata/frozen/README.md)
